text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 — egress failures observed in eu-west-1 (az-b). Healthchecks: NAT gateway in az-b reporting intermittent SNAT failures; ~25% of flows dropped. Pager: burton (oncall). Please acknowledge and join.

burton (oncall): acked. pulling logs now. oncall here.

alice (infra): I see a config change landed ~10m ago from ci/terraform: `networking:rev-20240328` — there is an updated NACL on private-subnet-azb that now has an explicit egress DENY on ports 1024-65535. that would break ephemeral return sockets.

burton (oncall): that matches. CloudWatch SNAT error spikes around 2041234400. can someone paste the terraform diff?

alice (infra): diff snip: ```hcl
# before: allow ephemeral
egress {
  protocol = "-1"
  rule_no = 100
  action = "allow"
  cidr_block = "0.0.0.0/0"
}
# after: deny ephemeral (bug)
egress {
  protocol = "tcp"
  from_port = 1024
  to_port = 65535
  rule_no = 100
  action = "deny"
  cidr_block = "0.0.0.0/0"
}
```

carla (sre): oof. that would absolutely kill return flows for NAT. are we confident rollback is safe? any other AZs affected?

sam (eng-runtime): only az-b NACL got the change. az-a/az-c still fine. traffic should route to other AZs if cross-az load balancing in place but we have sticky routes for some subnets so some hosts pinned to az-b. customer impact: webhook delivery and third-party API calls failing/timeouting for a subset of requests.

burton (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) emergency revert NACL change (terraform rollback) 2) temporary workaround: create a nat-instance in az-b and switch the route table for private-subnet-azb to point at instance (quick). 3) monitor for drop rate recovery and customer errors. I'll start step 2 while infra prepares rollback.

alice (infra): I'll kick a rollback apply now with `TF_VAR_force_rollback=true` — running in non-blocking mode. patching NACL to re-add ephemeral allow. ETA ~2m for plan, ~6m for apply.

mike (prod-svcs): posting customer impact note: engineering metrics show 12% of outgoing webhook attempts in eu-west-1 failing with 504/ETIMEDOUT. Customer-facing alerting: some customers may see delayed delivery or webhook retries. not a full outage but elevated error rate.

burton (oncall): starting temporary nat-instance in az-b: ```
aws ec2 run-instances --image-id ami-nat-2023 --instance-type t3.medium --subnet-id subnet-azb-private --associate-public-ip-address --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=instance,Tags=[{Key=Purpose,Value=emergency-nat}]'
```

carla (sre): oncall handoff in 10m. burton, please include instance id and route table changes in the handoff message. I'll verify rollback once apply completes and then supervise traffic shift back.

burton (oncall): instance up: i-0fakedemo1234, EIP assoc 52.86.1.23. updating route table rtb-0azbpriv -> target: i-0fakedemo1234. ```
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0azbpriv --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --instance-id i-0fakedemo1234
```

alice (infra): rollback apply finished at 2041234705. NACL now has ephemeral allow restored. verifying rules: `0.0.0.0/0 tcp 1024-65535 ALLOW` present.

sam (eng-runtime): metrics: SNAT failure rate dropped from 25% -> 3% within 30s of route change. webhook failure rate for eu-west-1 down to baseline 1.5% after 90s.

burton (oncall): handoff to carla incoming. burton -> carla: handoff notes: temporary nat-instance i-0fakedemo1234 created and route table rtb-0azbpriv pointed to it. terraform rollback for NACL applied (change set id tf-apply-789). monitoring shows recovery. I'm going offline in 8m. :thumbsup:

carla (sre): taking it. thanks burton. next steps: 1) terminate emergency nat instance after verification and route tables restored to nat-gw when healthy; 2) run full TF plan audit and block PRs touching NACLs until we have guardrails; 3) postmortem with timeline and CI gating fix. 4) notify customer ops with impact summary.

mike (prod-svcs): writing customer ops blurb now: "We experienced elevated outbound failures in eu-west-1 for ~10m due to a network config change that inadvertently blocked ephemeral ports on a private subnet. The team reverted the change and applied a temporary NAT instance; automated systems report request success rates recovered to normal. We will follow up with a postmortem and remediation timeline."

carla (sre): we should also add a pre-apply policy check to TF that rejects NACL denies that match ephemeral port blocks for private subnets. filing ticket: INF-4721.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: SEV2 resolved at 2041234920 — egress error rates returned to baseline and rollback confirmed. Incident channel archived.

carla (sre): closing the thread here. postmortem owners: alice, burton, carla. linking to PM when ready. :wave:
